action: General advice: patients should check with the hospital about any postponed appointments. Other hospitals should confirm they can run emergency care without IT and that backups are kept offline.
exec: An attack on hospital IT interrupted emergency care, showing the patient-safety stakes of IT resilience.
impact: Emergency room unavailable from 15 November; Freie Presse reported on 17 November that it is taking patients again.
plain: A cyberattack on a district hospital in Greiz, Germany, discovered on November 15, closed its emergency room. By November 17 it was reported to be taking patients again. The hospital has not said whether patient data was affected; police are investigating.
summary: The Greiz district says a cyberattack on its hospital was discovered on Sunday, November 15, made the emergency room unavailable, and that the state criminal police and prosecutors were called in. The district calls it an extortion attempt, Kommunal.de reports; the clinic gives no information on patient data. Freie Presse reported on November 17 that the emergency room is taking patients again; Security Affairs, citing MDR, says police are investigating a suspect.
title: Cyberattack closes emergency room at Greiz-Ronneburg hospital in Germany
